comparison: Perfect agreement on FRAP assay findings (C15, C16). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the conclusion that remaining TZPs maintain functional gap junction communication. OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment while peer review offers implicit acceptance through overall positive evaluation.

Perfect agreement on EdU proliferation control (C17). Both evaluations support this negative control ruling out proliferation differences. OpenEval explicitly notes this appropriately excludes an alternative explanation, while peer reviewers implicitly accept through comprehensive positive assessment.

Perfect agreement on claims C37-C38 regarding mRNA levels and mechanistic interpretation. Both support the finding that certain mRNAs are not depleted. OpenEval notes the speculation is appropriately cautious, while peer reviewers accept both data and alternative explanations without critique.

Strong agreement on TZP counting in intact and denuded GOCs (C10-C14). Both evaluations support these findings with statistical significance. OpenEval emphasizes the differential reduction pattern's mechanistic importance, while peer reviewers unanimously accept the data as convincing without questioning the interpretation.

Strong agreement on trajectory analysis (C29-C31). Both support the finding that TZP tips are closer to oocyte in SMAD4-depleted cells. OpenEval notes appropriate handling of non-significant orientation trend, peer reviewers accept the data as supporting the proposed mechanism.

Divergent evaluation of mechanistic model (C80-C83). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the model is plausible but lacks direct experimental validation of adhesion strength changes. Peer reviewers explicitly SUPPORT the model, with Reviewer 2 stating it is 'well supported by their experimental evidence.'

Agreement on SMAD4 depletion validation (C5-C9), though peer result R1 covers broader scope including C1-C4, C32. Both strongly support the multi-method validation approach. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of mRNA and protein evidence with statistical rigor, peer reviewers affirm methodology and conclusions are solid.

Agreement on luteinization control (C87). Both support the finding that luteinization markers are not increased in vitro, ruling out this alternative explanation. OpenEval notes this appropriately excludes confounding, peer reviewers implicitly accept through overall positive assessment.

Agreement on interpretation of TZP formation capacity (C93). Both support the conclusion that SMAD4-depleted cells can still generate TZPs. OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of uncertainty about generation rate, peer reviewers accept the mechanistic distinction between stability and initiation.

Agreement on N-cadherin and Notch2 protein reduction (C33, C34, C36). Both support these key mechanistic findings. OpenEval notes intriguing protein-mRNA discordance suggesting post-transcriptional regulation, peer reviewers accept as central to proposed model without questioning the mechanism.

Agreement on 3D image analysis of individual cells (C18-C20, C23). Both support the rigorous quantification showing 35% TZP reduction per cell. OpenEval emphasizes cell-autonomous effect and statistical rigor, Reviewer 3 specifically praises the 3D observation approach as 'solid.'

Agreement on reaggregation assay findings (C24-C26). Both support the 50% reduction in newly formed TZPs demonstrating effect on de novo formation. OpenEval notes importance for mechanistic interpretation, peer reviewers accept as part of solid 3D observation methodology.

Agreement on TZP morphometric measurements (C27, C28). Both support these detailed measurements from reaggregation experiments. OpenEval notes modest biological significance despite statistical significance, peer reviewers accept morphometric findings as part of solid 3D analysis.

Agreement on SMAD protein expression patterns (C1, C2). Both support immunoblot findings across follicular stages. OpenEval emphasizes convergence with prior literature, peer reviewers include these claims in comprehensive affirmation of methodology without specific concerns.

Agreement on Cre line validation (C3, C4). Both support FACS and immunostaining data showing low GFP-positive granulosa cells. OpenEval notes consistency with prior reports establishing unsuitability, peer reviewers include in overall acceptance of solid methodology.

Agreement on TZP length and width measurements (C21, C22). Both support these morphometric findings. OpenEval characterizes changes as statistically significant but biologically modest, peer reviewers accept detailed measurements as part of solid 3D observation without questioning biological interpretation.

Agreement on protein-mRNA discordance (C35). Both support the finding that mRNA levels are unchanged despite protein reduction. OpenEval highlights this as intriguing evidence for post-transcriptional regulation, peer reviewers accept without questioning the unexpected result.

Agreement on SMAD4 protein depletion (C32). Both support the 73.5% reduction shown by immunoblot. OpenEval includes this as part of protein-level validation, peer reviewers include in comprehensive affirmation that depletion strategy and validation are solid.

OpenEval rates mechanistic speculation (C84-C85) as UNCERTAIN, noting contradiction between literature linking SMAD4 to Cdh2 transcription and authors' own data showing no mRNA change. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific mechanistic uncertainty.

OpenEval supports claims C88-C90 about SMAD4 amplifying innate filopodia capacity, noting C90 is speculative interpretation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this comparative speculation about filopodia-generating capacity.

OpenEval supports synthesis of GDF9 and SMAD4 evidence (C94-C96) showing convergent effects on TZP organization. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this integration of current study with prior GDF9 depletion literature.

OpenEval supports justification for in vitro approach (C97) to avoid confounding luteinization effects. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this methodological justification, though peer R12 addresses related luteinization control.
